- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 2–3% below true peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and model forecasts rising, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- Model often underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases; add 1–2% to forecast for final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If model forecast is below 68.0 and sentiment is positive, increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid underestimating momentum.
- If model forecast is above 75.0 and sentiment is negative, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overcorrection or overestimation of decline.
- Model tends to lag in capturing sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.7) and model is flat, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid missing medium-term momentum.
